What the Grady County Clerk does

The Grady County Clerk is the county's recorder. The office files warranty deeds, mortgages and oil and gas leases, and it also runs county accounts payable, employee pay and purchasing. After a home sale closes, the deed ends up here. Until it is recorded, the public record still shows the old owner.

Land records are computerized from 1929 to the present. You can search them online at OKCountyRecords.com, though fees apply there. The courthouse in Chickasha is itself on the National Register of Historic Places.

Recording fees

Recording a conforming document costs $18 for the first page and $2 for each page after that. The $18 is $8 for recording plus a $10 preservation fee.

Grady County Clerk fees
Filing or serviceFee
First page, conforming document$18 ($8 plus $10 preservation)
Each additional page$2
First page, non-conforming document$25, plus $10 preservation
Each additional page, non-conforming$10
Copy$1 per page
Certified copy$1 per document
Documentary stamps$1.50 per $1,000

The office takes cash and checks if you give a correct address and a current phone number. It does not take temporary checks.

What makes a document conforming

A conforming page has a 2-inch margin at the top, 1-inch margins on the other three sides, and dark, legible print. A page that fails the test moves from $18 to $25 on page one and from $2 to $10 on each added page.

Two more filing rules catch sellers off guard:

  • The clerk needs a notarized original with original signatures, or a certified copy of an original.
  • A certified copy is stamped and sealed, and nothing can be added to it and refiled.

A title company that prepares your deed normally handles the format. Owners who draft their own deed for a family transfer or a quick sale are the ones most likely to pay the higher rate.

Documentary stamp tax

Stamps are due on any deed where money or other consideration changes hands. The clerk charges $1.50 per thousand dollars of price, and a chart in the office shows common amounts.

That rate equals the state's. Under 68 O.S. 3201 the tax is 75 cents for each $500 of consideration, or any fractional part, when the amount is more than $100, and it reaches only conveyances of realty that are sold. Every instrument filed must either pay the stamps or show its exemption on its face.

The clerk recommends attaching a bill of sale or a contract as proof of the price.

How fast a document is filed

A document delivered between 8 am and 4 pm is filed that day. Anything presented after 4 pm is filed the next day. Getting the document back takes seven to ten days.

The office scans every document and does not keep the original. Because of storage limits it stopped making shelf books at Book 4000, but all images are held online and backed up two ways. If you need the document right away, ask for a certified copy once it is filed, or use the online index.

  • Bring the full legal description.
  • Bring the closing statement for the stamp calculation.
  • Ask whether a DD-214 discharge record needs filing in the same visit, since the clerk's office files those too.

DD-214 records are not public. Only the service member, a spouse, children, the VA or a court order can open them.

Recording after a cash sale

A cash sale follows the same recording path as any other sale, with fewer lender steps ahead of it. Once buyer and seller sign, the deed goes to the clerk with proof of price and payment of the stamps.

  1. Confirm the legal description against your last recorded deed.
  2. Sign the deed in front of a notary, since the clerk needs a notarized original.
  3. Attach a closing statement, bill of sale or contract as proof of price.
  4. Work out documentary stamps at $1.50 per thousand, or state the exemption on the deed.
  5. Deliver the deed by 4 pm to have it filed the same day.

Many Grady County deeds describe ranch or farm tracts. Those descriptions run longer than a town lot and can push a deed past one page, which adds $2 for each extra page.

What to bring to the counter

Walk in with a short stack and the visit goes quickly. You want the signed, notarized original deed, the closing statement or contract that shows the price, a payment that matches the page count, and a correct return address and phone number. Add a bill of sale if the price is not on the closing statement. If you are filing a mortgage or an oil and gas lease along with the deed, keep each document separate, since the fee is figured per document.

Ask the clerk to confirm the page count before you pay. A deed that runs to a second page costs $2 more, or $10 more if the format fails, and it is easier to fix a margin at the counter than after the document is accepted.

Reading the record on older farm land

Grady County was organized in 1907. Before statehood, most of it belonged to the Chickasaw Nation, and the 1898 Curtis Act began the allotment process that turned communal land into individual parcels. Those allotments are the start of many deed chains here.

That history matters when you list a farm or ranch tract. A title search may run back to an allottee, and the description may refer to a quarter section instead of a lot and block. Check your description against the last recorded deed before the new one is typed, and keep the closing statement ready for the stamp calculation.

Checks before you record

Make sure the legal description on the deed matches the one in your last recorded deed. A typo can mean a corrective deed and a second recording fee. Many sales here involve older houses and acreage, with a median build year of 1981, so confirm that your own deed was recorded before you sell. Fixing any gap before closing speeds things up.

Property tax is a separate office. The Grady County Treasurer collects it, so request the balance there before the closing date.

Old farm deeds can trace back to Chickasaw allotments, so a title search on an older tract may run back to an allottee rather than a land patent. If the chain looks broken, tell your title company early. Towns like Chickasha, Minco, Verden, Rush Springs and Tuttle each turn up in deed descriptions, and the clerk's online index can be searched to see how your property was described the last time it changed hands.

Frequently asked questions

How much does the Grady County Clerk charge to record a deed?

The charge is $18 for the first page and $2 for each additional page, which includes an $8 recording fee and a $10 preservation fee. A non-conforming document costs $25 for the first page and $10 for each additional page, plus the $10 preservation fee.

What is the documentary stamp rate in Grady County?

The clerk charges $1.50 per thousand dollars of consideration, equal to 75 cents per $500 under 68 O.S. 3201. It applies when the price is more than $100, and every deed must pay it or state its exemption.

Can I record a copy of a deed in Grady County?

Only a notarized original with original signatures, or a certified copy of an original, can be filed. A plain photocopy is not accepted.

How long until I get my recorded deed back?

Expect seven to ten days. Documents delivered by 4 pm are filed that day, and later ones are filed the next day.

What does a copy of a recorded document cost in Grady County?

A plain copy is $1 per page, and a certified copy is $1 per document.

What the McClain County Clerk does

The McClain County Clerk is the registrar of deeds, one of eight elected county officials. The office keeps deeds, mortgages, plats, mineral interests, liens, court judgments, tax liens, oil and gas leases, powers of attorney and trust agreements. The clerk also serves as secretary to the Board of County Commissioners, the Excise Board, the Tax Roll Correction Board and the Equalization Board.

The office is at 121 North 2nd Avenue in Purcell. The mailing address is PO Box 629, Purcell, OK 73080. Land records can be reached at 405-527-3360, and hours are 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM. A DD-214 military discharge is recorded free for the veteran.

McClain County is in central Oklahoma, with Purcell as the seat. Its commuter towns draw buyers from the Oklahoma City and Norman area, and the median home value is $233,900.

Recording fees

The standard rate is $18.00 for the first page, which includes $8.00 for recording and $10.00 for preservation, plus $2.00 for each added page. A document that misses the statutory format rules costs more.

McClain County Clerk recording fees
Filing or serviceFee
First page, standard$18.00
Each additional page$2.00
First page, non-conforming$25.00 plus $10.00 preservation
Each additional page, non-conforming$10.00
Plat of one block or less$10.00
Plat of more than one block$25.00
Certifying a copy, per page$1.00
Mechanics or materialmen's lien$10.00

The schedule rests on 28 O.S. 32, and the non-conforming rate comes from subsection C of 19 O.S. 298. Mortgage recording and re-filing may involve fees payable to the County Treasurer, so call that office if you are recording a mortgage.

Documentary stamp tax

The clerk applies $0.75 for each $500 of the purchase price, rounded up to the next $500, and only when the price is above $100. The county website has a calculator that does the rounding for you.

Proof of price must come with the deed. A closing statement, a notarized bill of sale or an affidavit of purchase price all work. The clerk uses them only to compute the tax, and they are not recorded. If the transfer is exempt, the exemption has to appear on the face of the deed.

Under 68 O.S. 3201, the tax reaches only conveyances of realty that are sold.

Searching McClain County land records

The OKCountyRecords index shows data and scanned images from January 1980, with new records added in real time. The office preserves property records going back to the original U.S. land grants, so older records are held there even though the online index starts later.

You can search online by name, book and page, instrument type, recording dates and legal description, including quarter, section, township and range. That helps on rural land, where a deed may describe a quarter section instead of a lot and block.

Printed copies carry fees on the online site, and the revenue supports the county. Before you list, pull your last vesting deed and any mortgage releases, so gaps in the chain show up early.

Preparing to record a deed

Gather the signed and notarized deed, a closing statement or affidavit of purchase price, and a clear legal description. Then check the format, since a non-conforming page adds cost.

  1. Match the legal description to the last recorded deed.
  2. Prepare proof of the purchase price for the stamp tax.
  3. Check for any exemption and write it on the deed.
  4. Deliver the deed to 121 North 2nd Avenue in Purcell, or ask your title company to do so.
  5. Request a tax balance from the McClain County Treasurer, at 405-527-3261.

Special assessments such as sewer, water, weed, cleaning, paving and nuisance abatement charges are certified to the Treasurer once they turn delinquent, and they become a lien on the real estate account. They can show up long after the city sent its notice, so ask for a full account printout.

What the clerk's stamp calculator does for you

Rounding is where sellers slip. The tax moves in steps of $500, and any amount over a step rounds up to the next one, so a price a few dollars over a round number pays for a full extra step. The county website has a calculator for this, and using it before you go to the counter means you arrive with the right amount in hand.

Keep the proof of price in the same folder as the deed. The clerk looks at the closing statement, notarized bill of sale or affidavit only to compute the tax, then hands it back, so a copy is enough for your own records. If your transfer is exempt, write the exemption on the deed itself and do not rely on a separate note.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy McClain County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Reading a rural legal description

Much of the county is rural, so many deeds describe a quarter section, township and range instead of a lot and block. When you prepare a deed for a farm or acreage, copy the description from your last vesting deed word for word, then compare it against the online index, where you can search by quarter, section, township and range. A small difference in a direction or a number is the kind of error that leads to a corrective deed.

The west of the county is hilly and the southeastern arm is level lowland, so acreage can vary a great deal from one tract to the next. That makes the legal description, not the address, the thing buyers and title companies rely on.

Common seller situations

Sellers here hold either a commuter-town house near the Canadian River crossing or a rural tract with acreage. The stamp tax grows with the price, though the rate stays the same.

  • Inherited property where heirs live away from Purcell.
  • Land with mineral interests, which the clerk records separately.
  • Houses with lien or assessment questions.
  • Deeds that failed the format test and need to be redone.

With inherited land, settle who signs the deed before you schedule a closing, and bring the paperwork that shows the signers have authority to sell. For mineral interests, ask the Clerk how they were recorded, since they are filed apart from the surface deed.

A cash sale follows the same recording steps as any other sale, with fewer lender requirements ahead of it. The deed still needs notarized signatures, proof of price and the correct format, and the Treasurer's balance still has to be paid from the proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the McClain County Clerk's office?

It is at 121 North 2nd Avenue in Purcell, with a mailing address of PO Box 629, Purcell, OK 73080. Land records can be reached at 405-527-3360, and the office is open from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM.

What is the recording fee in McClain County?

The standard rate is $18.00 for the first page, made up of $8.00 for recording and $10.00 for preservation, plus $2.00 for each added page. Non-conforming documents cost $25.00 for the first page, $10.00 for each added page and a $10.00 preservation fee.

How is documentary stamp tax figured in McClain County?

The tax is $0.75 per $500 of the purchase price, rounded up, and applies when the price is above $100. Bring a closing statement, notarized bill of sale or affidavit of purchase price as proof of price.

Are McClain County land records online?

Yes. The OKCountyRecords site shows indexed data and scanned images from January 1980, and new records are added in real time. Printed copies carry fees.

Who do I call for a McClain County tax balance?

Call the McClain County Treasurer at 405-527-3261. The Clerk records deeds but does not collect property tax.
